Amber dusk settles over a sparse, decaying industrial district. Deep blue-black shadows and hazy air stretch across a flat, largely featureless pale-beige ground plane between isolated structures. Thin, hazy silhouettes of a modern city skyline frame the distant edges.

A broad elevated roadway runs lengthwise on regular concrete piers, its unusually bright, plain deck dominating aerial views. Diagonally across and beneath it passes a narrower rusted steel rail viaduct, exposed trusses carrying dark tracks. Roughly twenty-five brick warehouses, workshops, and tenement-like blocks gather along both corridors, separated by broad empty lots and unfinished-looking gaps.

Most buildings are rectangular and two to four stories tall. Red or faded tan brick, weathered plaster patches, repetitive dark windows, flat or gently pitched rust-streaked roofs, and occasional decorative cornices define them. Several larger freestanding mill buildings stand around the outer area; smaller sheds pack near the central crossing. Wooden utility poles and dense sagging overhead wires follow the streets. Beneath the viaduct lie chain-link fencing and graffiti-covered metal barriers. Exterior fire escapes, narrow catwalks, suspended industrial pipes, rooftop vents, service doors, steps, and shadowed passages between buildings complete the industrial detail.

Streets and yards stay empty of people and vehicles, with no vegetation and little visible surface detailing. Low-rise, fragmented, and irregularly spaced, the reconstructed district is denser around the rail junction and markedly emptier toward the perimeter.

deterministic_rule_draft.prompt:
Amber dusk settles over a sparse, decaying industrial district. Deep blue-black shadows and hazy air stretch across a flat, largely featureless pale-beige ground plane between isolated structures. Thin, hazy silhouettes of a modern city skyline frame the distant edges.

A broad elevated roadway runs lengthwise on regular concrete piers, its unusually bright, plain deck dominating aerial views. Diagonally across and beneath it passes a narrower rusted steel rail viaduct, exposed trusses carrying dark tracks. Roughly twenty-five brick warehouses, workshops, and tenement-like blocks gather along both corridors, separated by broad empty lots and unfinished-looking gaps.

Most buildings are rectangular and two to four stories tall. Red or faded tan brick, weathered plaster patches, repetitive dark windows, flat or gently pitched rust-streaked roofs, and occasional decorative cornices define them. Several larger freestanding mill buildings stand around the outer area; smaller sheds pack near the central crossing. Wooden utility poles and dense sagging overhead wires follow the streets. Beneath the viaduct lie chain-link fencing and graffiti-covered metal barriers. Exterior fire escapes, narrow catwalks, suspended industrial pipes, rooftop vents, service doors, steps, and shadowed passages between buildings complete the industrial detail.

Streets and yards stay empty of people and vehicles, with no vegetation and little visible surface detailing. Low-rise, fragmented, and irregularly spaced, the reconstructed district is denser around the rail junction and markedly emptier toward the perimeter.
